hints: A rooted tree is determined by the multiset of its rooted child subtrees.
Assign equal IDs to identical sorted lists of child IDs.
Compare the IDs of the two roots, using the same ID dictionary for both trees.
analogy: Describe each branch by a label derived from the sorted labels of its smaller branches.
example: A root with two leaf children is isomorphic to another root with two leaves, regardless of vertex labels.
algorithm: Process each rooted tree bottom-up. For each vertex sort the IDs of its children and intern that list in a shared dictionary, obtaining the same ID for equal lists. Compare the IDs at the two roots. Use iterative traversal if needed for deep trees.
correctness: Leaves share the empty-list ID. Inductively, two rooted subtrees receive the same ID exactly when their child-subtree multisets match, which is precisely rooted tree isomorphism.
complexity: For n vertices per pair, O(n log n) time with ordered interning and O(n) space, apart from representation overhead.
